source.check: unopposed members and full names from the News-Letter's list of nominations (6 May; * = retiring member as printed there) and its list of the remaining contests after withdrawals (7 May); votes, majorities, spoiled papers and electorates read on the page image of the News-Letter's results

note: First May round under the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1934 (no election in January 1935): one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the 1932 cohort) and the eight aldermen elected in 1929 (Clifton, Court, Cromac, Dock, Falls, Shankill, Victoria, Windsor); nominations Tuesday 5 May, poll Friday 15 May 1936. After the withdrawal in Dock, 17 of the 23 seats were filled unopposed; Clifton, Court (both seats), Duncairn, Falls and Smithfield were contested (Belfast News-Letter, 6, 7 and 16 May 1936). Mercer, a retiring councillor, was the official Unionist nominee for the aldermanship vacated by Alderman J. W. Nixon; W. M. Wilton withdrew his opposition (News-Letter, 6 May 1936). The Irish News, 16 May 1936, p. 7, prints the same poll (Mercer 3,649, "S. Hazlett" 723, 191 spoiled, total poll 4,563, which adds up). The Belfast Corporation register of members (PRONI LA/7/1/CA/1/3) records Mercer as unopposed, as it does the other seven aldermen of 1936; both newspapers print the poll.
